soul_sand.analogue: Loose silty, organic-rich sand: slows entities, so a looser and more damped granular bed than sand.

provenance.absorption: derived: random-incidence (Paris integral) absorption of a 1 m locally reacting layer on rigid backing, Miki impedance with sigma = 150000 Pa s/m2 and phi = 0.45.
provenance.scattering: estimated: mid-band (500/1000 Hz) s = 0.25 chosen from surface relief, expanded with a fixed band shape [0.35,0.45,0.65,0.85,1.15,1.4,1.6,1.7] x s_mid, clamped 0.05-0.95 (Odeon-style single-value expansion; shape is an assumption).
provenance.transmission_loss: derived: two parallel paths, tau = tau_air + tau_frame. Air path: rigid-frame equivalent fluid (Miki 1990, sigma = 150000 Pa s/m2, Zc divided by porosity phi = 0.45). Frame path: lossy layer with bulk rho = 1400, frame speed 150 m/s (estimated), eta = 0.2. Diffuse field 0-78 deg (oblique kz = sqrt(k^2 - kx^2)), 61 frequencies per octave. Miki is fitted for 0.01 < f/sigma < 1; outside that range values are extrapolated.
provenance.gameplay_transmission_loss: design: Gcap*(1-exp(-TL_real/Gcap)), Gcap = 45 dB. One full block of dense material gives ~28-42 dB (faint), and three blocks give >85 dB (inaudible).
provenance.bulk: sound_speed_m_s is the FRAME (skeleton) wave speed, estimated; airborne sound inside the pores travels at roughly 200-340 m/s. Also soul soil.

sources: Miki, Y. (1990) 'Acoustical properties of porous materials - modifications of Delany-Bazley models', J. Acoust. Soc. Jpn (E) 11(1):19-24; Delany & Bazley (1970) Applied Acoustics 3:105-116 (equations recalled from the papers, not re-fetched)

Shallow dry sand P-wave 87-390 m/s (KFUPM dune study) - https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/p-wave-velocity-at-shallow-depths-in-sand-dunes-and-its-effect-on/ ; surface alluvium 180-255 m/s (Steeples et al., GRL 26(2):279) - https://kuscholarworks.ku.edu/bitstream/1808/17259/1/SteeplesD_GRL_26(2)279.pdf

Normal-incidence transmission through a homogeneous layer between two identical fluids: tau = |cos(kd) + (i/2)(Z2/Z1 + Z1/Z2) sin(kd)|^-2 (standard result, e.g. Kinsler et al., Fundamentals of Acoustics); complex k and Z from loss factor

sculk.analogue: Soft, hydrated biological tissue (rho ~1050, c ~1540 m/s, the standard soft-tissue value) with a velvety fibrous surface. Damping is set high because sculk 'absorbs' vibrations in lore.

provenance.absorption: Invented: a fuzzy organic mat over tissue, rising with frequency like a thin fibrous layer.
provenance.scattering: estimated: mid-band (500/1000 Hz) s = 0.3 chosen from surface relief, expanded with a fixed band shape [0.35,0.45,0.65,0.85,1.15,1.4,1.6,1.7] x s_mid, clamped 0.05-0.95 (Odeon-style single-value expansion; shape is an assumption).
provenance.transmission_loss: derived: diffuse-field (0-78 deg, Paris-weighted) transmission through a homogeneous lossy layer in air, 61 frequencies per octave. Below the first thickness resonance f = c/(2d): coherent layer formula tau(theta) = |cos(kz d) + (i/2)(Zt/Z0t + Z0t/Zt) sin(kz d)|^-2 with complex k = omega/(c*sqrt(1+i*eta)) (includes tunnelling beyond the critical angle). Above it: incoherent energy model tau = t1^2*A/(1-(1-t1)^2*A^2), t1 = 4*Z1*Z2/(Z1+Z2)^2 per interface (zero beyond the air-to-fluid critical angle), A = exp(-2*alpha*d/cos(theta_t)). Between fres/2 and 2*fres the two are blended linearly in log-frequency (a smoothing choice to remove a model-switch step, not physics). Real water/lava bodies are not plane-parallel, so their sharp coherent resonances are not physical at block scale.
provenance.gameplay_transmission_loss: design: Gcap*(1-exp(-TL_real/Gcap)), Gcap = 45 dB. One full block of dense material gives ~28-42 dB (faint), and three blocks give >85 dB (inaudible).
provenance.bulk: All sculk blocks, sensors, shrieker and catalyst.

water_fresh.provenance: speed: derived, Marczak (1997) pure-water polynomial at 10 C (20 C also given). absorption: derived, Ainslie & McColm (1998) with S = 0 (only the viscous pure-water term remains). Interface loss: derived, 10log10((Z1+Z2)^2/(4 Z1 Z2)) at normal incidence. Gameplay absorption: design value; real absorption is negligible over Minecraft distances, so the underwater 'muffle' must come from interface loss plus this low-pass.

water_sea.provenance: speed: derived, Mackenzie (1981) at 10 C, 35 ppt, surface. absorption: derived, Ainslie & McColm (1998), T = 10 C, S = 35, pH 8, depth 0 (boric acid + MgSO4 relaxations + viscous). Use for ocean biomes if you want; the difference is inaudible at game scale.

lava.provenance: density and bubble-free speed: ESTIMATED (basaltic melt ~2600-2750 kg/m3 and ~2300-2900 m/s at ~1200 C; literature values not retrieved this session, low confidence). absorption: derived classical viscous absorption alpha = omega^2*(4/3*mu)/(2*rho*c^3) with mu = 100 Pa s, which is a lower bound: real lava's crystals and bubbles scatter and absorb far more. Bubbly speed: derived from Wood's equation with 1% gas (rho 0.2, c 700 m/s), the mechanism in Kieffer (1977). Gameplay absorption: design value (lava should swallow sound within a few blocks).

acoustic_fill_notes: Fraction of the block cell cross-section that blocks sound. Per-band cell transmission: tau_cell = (1 - fill) + fill * 10^(-TL/10), so TL_cell = -10*log10(tau_cell). 0 = acoustically transparent (ignore for occlusion; no collision shape, or a small prop). Listed values override the collision shape because it would mislead (no shape at all, or a solid-looking shape full of holes: bars, chains, grates, spawners, fences, scaffolding, ladders, cobwebs). Blocks not listed: derive coverage from the collision VoxelShape, using transmission_loss_db_thin for thin parts and transmission_loss_db_1m scaled by thickness for thick parts. All fill values are estimates.
